messages:
Alex R.: Heads-up — saw a near-miss this morning: 5xx/Throttling from AWS KMS during a key rotation attempt, caused a cascading retry spike in the encrypt path. triggered `kms-throttle-high` alert from the infra runbook bot.
Maria G.: Ugh. any user impact? latency or errors surfaced to customers?
Alex R.: No customer-facing errors, but internal latency SLOs for small-sync inference calls spiked ~800ms -> 2s because we blocked on `GenerateDataKey` calls. Retries piled up and increased queuing.
Jeff L.: Can you paste the log snippet?
Alex R.: Sure: ``[2025-06-01T09:12:34Z] ERROR encryptor.go:142 | kms: GenerateDataKey failed: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
stack: runtime/goroutine  ...`` Also saw CloudWatch metric `ThrottledRequests` jump for our key alias `alias/redwood-data-prod` (region us-west-2).
Kat H.: Important context: our envelope flow does one `GenerateDataKey` per object write. With key rotation runs plus background re-encrypt jobs, that key got hammered.
sre-bot: Alert: kms-throttle-high (CW alarm) -> triggered 2025-06-01T09:11:00Z; suppressed after 15min by autoscaling.
Maria G.: So near-miss because retries kept requests alive instead of failing fast. We should avoid head-of-line blocking. What mitigations do we want short-term?
Jeff L.: Short-term: (1) add circuit-breaker around KMS calls so we fail fast after N concurrent failures, (2) tighten retries: exponential backoff + jitter and cap max attempts to 3, (3) implement local token-bucket limiting concurrent KMS requests per instance.
Alex R.: Agreed. Also increase local DEK cache TTL for reads where allowed: we already cache encrypted data keys (DEKs) for 15m; bump to 2h for hot objects to cut down GenerateDataKey frequency. We must confirm compliance: we never persist plaintext DEKs.
Kat H.: For envelope encryption clarifications: we cache the encrypted DEK (ciphertextBlob) alongside metadata. Decrypt only when node doesn't have a valid cached plaintext DEK, and plaintext DEK is zeroed after use. Increasing encrypted-DEK cache TTL is compliant. Document that in runbook.
Maria G.: Mid-term: (1) split heavy workloads to use a dedicated KMS CMK per subsystem / region to spread quota, (2) request AWS KMS limit increase / apply for higher throughput key type (multi-tenant KMS quotas are per-key by default), (3) consider using multi-region keys for geo failover.
Jeff L.: Long-term: explore hybrid model: use HSM-backed local key cache (customer-managed HSM or on-prem) for the highest QPS paths with envelope wrapping by KMS weekly instead of per-write. Need legal + compliance signoff.
Alex R.: Action items: Alex/R to push circuit-breaker + retry cap this afternoon (PR + rollout), Jeff to draft runbook edits for DEK caching and rotation constraints, Kat to prepare compliance note about encrypted-DEK caching and key rotation policy. Maria to open AWS support case for quota and get target ETA.
Kat H.: Also add observability: emit metrics `kms.calls.count`, `kms.calls.throttled`, `data_key.cache_hit` and create dashboard + CW alarm on throttled% > 2% over 5m.
Maria G.: I'll create the tickets and link the PRs. Tagging @Kat H. and @Jeff L. for approvals.
Alex R.: Quick config snippet for circuit-breaker (golang pseudocode): ``cb := gobreaker.NewCircuitBreaker(gobreaker.Settings{Interval:time.Minute, Timeout:30*time.Second, ReadyToTrip: func(counts gobreaker.Counts) bool { return counts.ConsecutiveFailures > 5 }})``
Jeff L.: Good. Also add a fallback path that returns a well-documented transient error to callers so frontends can degrade gracefully (not retry indefinitely).
Alex R.: Noted. We'll also add a playbook step: if KMS throttling happens during rotation, pause rotation job, reduce concurrency, and resume with lower concurrency.
Kat H.: I'll update the rotation tooling to support concurrency limits and resume tokens.
Maria G.: Thanks team — let's treat this as a near-miss postmortem (no P1) and aim to close action items within 2 weeks. I'll set a follow-up sync for next Monday. :thumbsup:
